title: bug: local-runner-bridge S11 (SIGTERM, pipes held) intermittently sees a live lingering child when the observation is written
description: CQ-M06 epic-final gate. At HEAD 0d913716, `node --test scripts/tests/*.test.mjs` in a Linux snapshot failed once (load average about 5). The failing test was "S11 after SIGTERM, the job's lingering child that holds the output pipes is killed before the one observation", at scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs:1261: report.dead was [true, false]. The file passed 3/3 alone and the full suite passed on rerun. Decide between two causes: a probe race, where done() (State Z, or SIGKILL in ShdPnd) misreads a process already mid-exit; or a real killpg-before-observation ordering gap in relay(). Then fix the probe or the relay. Evidence log: /tmp/moe-m06-gate.mpEtE8/logs/scripts-test4.log (may be cleaned).
definitionOfDone: The root cause is named: a probe race or a relay ordering gap, with evidence
S11 is deterministic under load, for example 50 consecutive runs of local-runner-bridge.test.mjs while another full suite runs, without weakening the 'killed before the one observation' invariant

implementationPlan.description:
DoD 1: re-verify and record the root cause before touching code. This step changes no file in the checkout.

First read comment-0fb39d4e on this task: the architect's repro and numbers.

In a scratch directory outside the checkout, write a standalone `python3 -I` script that mirrors the S11 'open' row N times:
- Make pipes (r, w) and (pr, pw), then fork J.
- J: os.setsid(), then fork C. C closes pw, sleeps 600 s holding w, then os._exit(0). J writes C's pid to pw, then os._exit(0).
- Parent: close w, read C's pid, os.waitpid(J, 0). C is now an orphan in group J.
- Parent: os.killpg(J, SIGKILL), using its own recorded group id and never a name match. Read r to EOF.
- Then read /proc/C/status and /proc/C/stat once each. Classify that one view with BOTH predicates:
  - today's: gone, State Z, or SIGKILL (0x100) in ShdPnd;
  - step 2's cannot_run: it adds State X, and PF_EXITING (0x4) in stat's flags, which is field [6] after the last ')'.
- Error handling: wrap each iteration so any exception killpg's that iteration's own recorded group before re-raising.

Run at least 2000 iterations under nice -n 19, at the box's normal load or under step 3's background load. Record `uptime`, the count of each first-probe view, today's alive count, and the fixed alive count. Expect today's alive count above 0, all of them 'X (dead)' with ShdPnd 0x0. The fixed alive count must be 0.

Name the root cause in a moe.add_comment on this task: a probe race in OBSERVE's done(), not a relay ordering gap. Include these numbers and this reasoning: on the 'open' row, pump() reaches stdout/stderr EOF only after the lingering child has run exit_files, and only pump's start-pipe killpg (scripts/local-runner/guest-supervisor.py:477) kills that child.

If the fixed predicate ever reads a view as alive, quote that view verbatim in the comment. Widen cannot_run in step 2 only by another fact proving the process can never run user code again, never by a retry or a sleep. If there is no such fact, call moe.report_blocked with the view.
implementationPlan.note: Root cause (probe race) recorded in comment; my replica (107k iters) never hit the X(dead) window, architect's repro did (5/2000). No checkout files changed. Dirty paths of other sessions untouched.

implementationPlan.description:
Test-only fix in scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs. Edit with the Edit tool only. scripts/local-runner/guest-supervisor.py stays byte-identical: relay() is sound.

(a) Above OBSERVE (its comment is at lines 1220-1221), add a CANNOT_RUN python snippet that OBSERVE and the new pin row share:
```
// What proc(5) shows of a process that can run no more: State Z (zombie) or X (its reaper is releasing it), SIGKILL
// pending in ShdPnd, or PF_EXITING (0x4) in /proc/<pid>/stat's flags, which is set as do_exit begins and never
// cleared. The pending sets read empty once the reaper releases a task, and status is no atomic snapshot, so status
// alone can read a dead process as live (task-b712ce09: 'X (dead)' with ShdPnd 0x0 on Linux 6.18).
const CANNOT_RUN = `import signal
def cannot_run(state, shdpnd, flags):
    return state[0] in 'ZX' or bool(int(shdpnd, 16) & (1 << signal.SIGKILL - 1)) or bool(flags & 0x4)
`;
```

(b) OBSERVE starts `${CANNOT_RUN}import base64, time`. Inside the same try, done(pid) reads status as it does today, plus `flags = int(open('/proc/%d/stat' % pid).read().rsplit(')', 1)[1].split()[6])`. FileNotFoundError and ProcessLookupError on either read still return True. It then returns `cannot_run(status['State'], status['ShdPnd'], flags)`. Keep the `\\t` escaping the template already uses. Reword OBSERVE's comment to 'whether that process can run no more: reaped, or CANNOT_RUN (Linux only; null elsewhere)'.

(c) After the S11 loop (after line 1272), add one deterministic row that starts no process:
- Title starts 'S11 probe:'; skip NO_GUEST.
- It runs python3 -I -c `${CANNOT_RUN}import json, sys\nprint(json.dumps([cannot_run(*v) for v in json.loads(sys.argv[1])]))` over these views, in order:
  - ['Z (zombie)','0000000000000000',0]
  - ['X (dead)','0000000000000000',0]
  - ['R (running)','0000000000000100',0]
  - ['R (running)','0000000000000000',4]
  - ['S (sleeping)','0000000000000000',0]
  - ['R (running)','0000000000000000',64]
  - ['S (sleeping)','0000000000004000',0]
- It asserts exit status 0 (message: its stderr) and deepEqual [true, true, true, true, false, false, false].

The last three views pin that a live process, PF_FORKNOEXEC (0x40) and a pending SIGTERM never count.

Leave LINGER, ENDINGS, the six S11 rows and every other test unchanged.

Error handling: the pin row asserts python's exit status with its stderr, so a syntax slip fails loudly. done() keeps its ESRCH/ENOENT handling.
implementationPlan.note: Added CANNOT_RUN snippet, rewired OBSERVE done(), added 'S11 probe' pin row. Edit tool only.

implementationPlan.description:
Adversarial self-review of the one-file diff. Check each of these:
- (a) scripts/local-runner/guest-supervisor.py has no diff, so relay() is unchanged.
- (b) Every clause of cannot_run states a fact that the process can never run user code again: zombie, released, SIGKILL pending, or in do_exit. None is a timing allowance such as a retry, a sleep or a grace period, any of which could hide a genuinely late kill.
- (c) M1 really failed the 'closed' rows on the dead/running assertions, not on a parse error.

comments.author: architect-98c94b4c
comments.content:
Architect evidence, 2026-11-01T23:05Z. Kernel 6.18.33.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2, uid 1000, load average 3.3-3.7. Root cause: a PROBE RACE in OBSERVE's done(). There is no relay ordering gap.

Repro (standalone python, scratch only; it kills only the process group it created, by recorded id). This mirrors the S11 'open' row:
- A setsid'd job forks a sleeping orphan that holds a pipe, then exits.
- The parent reaps the job, killpg's the group, reads the pipe to EOF, then reads /proc/<orphan>/status once, as done() does.

Results:
- 2000 iterations: today's predicate (State Z, or SIGKILL in ShdPnd) called the dead orphan alive 5 times. All 5 were 'X (dead)' with ShdPnd 0x0 and SigPnd 0x0. A fixed predicate that also accepts State X called it alive 0 times.
- The first-probe views also included 'Z' with ShdPnd 0x0 (3) and 'X' with ShdPnd SIGKILL (1). So State and the pending sets come from different instants: proc(5) status is no atomic snapshot, and the pending sets read empty once the system reaper releases the task.
- A separate run polled continuously from the kill until the orphan was gone, 400 kills. Every post-kill view was R+ShdPnd SIGKILL (+PF_EXITING), then Z+ShdPnd SIGKILL+PF_EXITING, then gone. The only view that looks alive is the reaper's X window.

Why it is not a relay gap: on the 'open' row, the lingering child holds the job's output pipes. pump() therefore sees stdout/stderr EOF only after that child has run exit_files in do_exit. The only thing that kills that child is pump's killpg at the start-pipe EOF (guest-supervisor.py:477). So the kill always precedes the observation, and the child was dead, mid-release, when done() read it.

The failing gate log /tmp/moe-m06-gate.mpEtE8/logs/scripts-test4.log:1423 still exists: report.dead [true, false], 67.5 ms.

comments.author: worker-9be3bcf5
comments.content:
Worker, step 1 (DoD 1). ROOT CAUSE: a probe race in OBSERVE's done(), NOT a relay ordering gap.

Reasoning from the source: on the 'open' row, pump() (guest-supervisor.py:466-481) reaches stdout/stderr EOF only after the lingering child has run exit_files, and only pump's start-pipe killpg (:477) kills that child. run_bridge then reaps the guard and only then writes the observation. So relay() has already killed the child before done() runs. done() reads /proc/<pid>/status once, and today's predicate accepts only gone, State Z, or SIGKILL in ShdPnd. Between do_exit's exit_files and the reaper's release, status can show 'X (dead)' with empty pending sets. proc(5) status is not an atomic snapshot, so State and ShdPnd can also come from different instants. The failing run's report.dead [true, false] is that view.

Repro numbers:
- Architect (comment-0fb39d4e), 2000 iterations at load 3.3 on 6.18.33.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2: today's predicate called the dead orphan alive 5 times, all 'X (dead)' with ShdPnd 0x0. A predicate that also accepts State X called it alive 0 times.
- Mine: a standalone `python3 -I` replica (/tmp/b712-scratch/repro.py, scratch only, kills only its own recorded group id) at load 3.6-5.7 under nice -n 19. It ran 3000 + 4x6000 + 10x8000 = 107000 iterations. Views: about 'gone' 99%, 'Z ShdPnd=0x100 PF_EXITING=1' about 1%, today's alive 0, fixed predicate (Z or X, SIGKILL pending, PF_EXITING) alive 0.
- My replica did NOT reproduce the 'X (dead)' window on this boot, so I have no first-hand today's-alive count above 0. The architect's 5/2000 and the CI failure are the evidence for the window. Mine only confirms the fixed predicate never reads a dead orphan as alive. Every view seen (gone, Z with PF_EXITING set) is in the fixed predicate's dead set.

Decision: proceed with the test-only probe fix plus the deterministic 'S11 probe' pin row, which does not depend on catching the race live. Each clause of the new predicate is a kernel fact that the process can never run user code again. No retry, sleep or grace period is added.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) Changing relay(), e.g. waiting for the job group to empty before the observation: rejected. The relay ordering is sound, because on the 'open' row EOF can only follow the child's exit_files, which only the start-pipe killpg causes. A production change for a probe artifact adds risk and latency. (2) A retry or sleep in done(): rejected. A timing allowance could hide a genuinely late kill, which weakens the invariant. (3) Accepting State X only: this is the minimal fix the evidence supports. But /proc/<pid>/status is not atomic: State and ShdPnd are rendered at different instants, so a preempted read can pair a pre-exit State with a post-release empty ShdPnd. PF_EXITING in /proc/<pid>/stat is set at do_exit entry and never cleared, so it closes that window with a fact rather than a timing allowance. (4) Requiring the /proc entry to vanish (reaped): rejected. The system reaper controls that, not relay().
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: OBSERVE computes `dead` inside its write_frame wrapper, before the observation bytes are written, so any dead indicator read during done() was already true at the write: each indicator is monotonic. Run non-root, GUARD skips CLONE_NEWPID, so the lingering child is reparented to the system reaper (WSL /init), whose wait and release create the X window. Architect repro, 2000 iterations at load 3.3 on 6.18.33.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2: today's predicate saw 5 alive-looking views, all 'X (dead)' with ShdPnd 0x0; the fixed predicate saw 0. A whole bridge file run takes about 19 s and needs no node_modules (node builtins only).
planningNotes.risks: Escaping: the python lives inside JS template literals, so the existing `\\t` stays doubled and `\n` in the pin row's -c string is a JS newline. The stress gate takes 20+ min of wall clock: use setsid + pidfile + a stop file and bounded waits (mem:gotcha-harness-snapshot-needs-full-archive), and never pattern-kill. Under M1 the 'open' rows each take 20 s, the spawnSync timeout; the GUARD life pipe and the rows' finally blocks clean up their groups. In a fresh snapshot without the daemon dist, the background scripts suite fails TY1 and C4-C9 fast. That is only load, but do not report those failures as regressions. The governor asked for nice -n 19 on both the load and the loop, with the load average recorded.

completionSummary: Root cause: a probe race in OBSERVE's done(), not a relay ordering gap. A dead lingering child can read 'X (dead)' with empty ShdPnd. The architect saw 5/2000 such views; my 107k-iteration replica never hit that window, and the fixed predicate read 0 alive. Fix, test-only in scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs (+32 lines): a shared CANNOT_RUN predicate that counts State Z or X, SIGKILL in ShdPnd, or PF_EXITING in /proc/<pid>/stat flags. OBSERVE.done() now uses it, and a new deterministic 'S11 probe:' row pins it. guest-supervisor.py, relay(), pump() and the six S11 rows are unchanged. The gate ran in a Linux git-archive snapshot under env -i and nice -n 19. The file passed once and again fresh at the end (90 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped). Mutants: M1 (pump killpg removed) fails all 6 S11 'after' rows (open: ETIMEDOUT; closed: 'a job process could still run'). M2 ('ZX' to 'Z') and M3 (PF_EXITING dropped) each fail the 'S11 probe' row on an assertion diff. Stress: 50 of 50 consecutive runs passed with a background scripts suite loop running. Load was 2.3 at start, 5.5/5.6/5.8/5.2/4.2 at runs 10-50. The background loop exited via its stop file and nothing was killed by name.
